question.question: Can VerifyLeader complete successfully using nonvoter confirmations when the leader has no confirmation from another voter, despite its threshold being derived from the voter set?
question.importance: False authority verification could permit callers to serve stale FSM reads after a voter majority has moved to a new leader. A local eligibility discrepancy is distinct from proving an end-to-end stale read.
contexts: fixed configuration with three voters and at least one nonvoter
one pending verification in leader tenure
event_paths: VerifyLeader -> leaderLoop -> verifyLeader -> peer notifyAll -> verifyFuture.vote -> leaderLoop response

supporting_behavior_ids.B-membership: Defines voter versus nonvoter eligibility and stable configuration.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-leader: Creates replication state for each configured peer and supplies separate lease/exit protection.

counterevidence: Lease check filters voters and may independently step down later; the schedule must not assume it is absent forever.
Leader exit aborts verification, and false callback can force rejection.
A local success would not alone demonstrate stale application data or a second leader.
unknowns: Does full public verification complete from nonvoter support under a legal bounded schedule before lease loss?
What precise responsibility applies to verification support membership independently of whole-cluster stale-read consequence?
question.trigger_rationale: Commitment and lease explicitly filter voters; verification registers all replState peers and passes only booleans to the tally. A small constructor-based check can distinguish real callback eligibility from an unseen alternate guard. This is more direct authority-safety work than the storage-error recovery lead, whose failure applicability and indefinite recovery remain less settled.
